inputs.original_text: Listen, this story from JFK International Airport in New York on Thursday really shows what strong authority and duty look like in practice. An Immigration and Customs Enforcement agent stepped in without hesitation when a baby in a crowded TSA line with his family stopped breathing. The Department of Homeland Security released video footage of the agent holding the child, spotting the crisis, and taking immediate action. This is the decisive responsibility we need to hold society together, protect families, and keep order when things turn chaotic and the vulnerable are exposed. These agents embody the values of personal duty and national protection that actually safeguard our children and way of life. It underscores why we must back our law enforcement and border institutions instead of tolerating progressive attacks that erode the traditions and structures keeping us secure.
inputs.modified_text: I heard about this story from JFK International Airport in New York on Thursday involving an Immigration and Customs Enforcement agent who stepped in to help a baby that stopped breathing while with his family in a crowded TSA line. The Department of Homeland Security released video footage of the agent holding the child and taking immediate action. But trying to use this to demand more support for law enforcement and border institutions while dismissing progressive calls for change completely misses the point. It actually draws attention to the structural inequalities and pressures that put vulnerable families in these chaotic, high-risk situations in the first place. We need real institutional reform focused on equity, protection of marginalized groups, and addressing historical patterns of discrimination rather than doubling down on enforcement systems that often expose people to harm.
